literature.headline_zh: 诺如病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期诺如病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 在 1,579 个 诺如病毒 暴发 中,有 1,225 个进行了基因分型。GII.4悉尼在2022年下半年(46.15%)和2023年(51.63%)占据主导地位,而GII.17[P17]在2024年下半年占据主导地位,造成暴发的75.28%。 [10.1186/s12879-026-14009-8]
该框架预测 诺如病毒 风险为 77.0%,与记录的 暴发 验证过程中记录的历史真实风险 79.3% 密切相关。 [10.1007/978-3-032-30805-4_5]
隔室模型虽然与平均模拟结果一致,但无法可靠地预测任何单个 暴发 事件。 [10.3390/appliedmath6070115]
该公式成功地推断出稀有基因型的适应性,这些基因型的流行程度比优势谱系低几个数量级。它在不同的数据集上表现强劲,包括条形码酵母 进化 实验、小鼠 诺如病毒-1 连续传代实验和 SARS-CoV-2 全球基因组 患病率 数据,证明了广泛的适用性。 [10.64898/2026.07.18.739367]
500 个海水样本中近一半 (44.0%) 的至少一种病毒目标检测呈阳性。病毒检出率多年来有所不同,可能受到与 COVID-19 大流行相关的流行病学动态的影响。系统发育分析表明,大多数环境病毒序列与先前在同一地区的人类临床病例中鉴定的毒株相同或密切相关。 [10.1038/s41598-026-62813-8]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: Among 1,579 norovirus outbreaks, 1,225 were genotyped. GII.4 Sydney dominated in the second halves of 2022 (46.15%) and 2023 (51.63%), while GII.17[P17] became predominant in the second half of 2024, causing 75.28% of outbreaks. [10.1186/s12879-026-14009-8]

The framework predicted a norovirus risk of 77.0%, closely aligning with the documented historical ground-truth risk of 79.3% during validation against a documented outbreak. [10.1007/978-3-032-30805-4_5]
The compartmental model, while consistent with average simulation outcomes, failed to reliably predict any single outbreak event. [10.3390/appliedmath6070115]
The formula successfully inferred fitnesses for rare genotypes several orders of magnitude less prevalent than dominant lineages. [10.64898/2026.07.18.739367]

Nearly half (44.0%) of the 500 marine water samples tested positive for at least one viral target. Viral detection rates varied across years, likely influenced by COVID-19 pandemic-associated epidemiological dynamics. [10.1038/s41598-026-62813-8]

papers.title: A new wave of resurge for GII.17[P17] norovirus in multiple provinces of China in 2024
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Noroviruses is a major cause of outbreaks and sporadic acute gastroenteritis (AGE) across all age groups. Although the GII.4 norovirus has been the primary cause of most AGE outbreaks, Non-GII.4 norovirus has been reported globally. AIM: We aimed to report an increase in GII.17 norovirus outbreaks of acute gastroenteritis in multiple provinces of China during the second half of 2024. METHODS: Data and specimens from AGE outbreaks (January 2022-December 2024) were collected. Samples were tested via real-time RT-PCR; positive GII.17[P17] samples underwent sequencing and phylogenetic analysis. RESULTS: Among 1,579 norovirus outbreaks, 1,225 were genotyped. The first halves of 2022-2024 saw co-circulation of genotypes GII.3[P12], GII.4 Sydney, GII.17[P17], and GII.7[P7]. GII.4 Sydney dominated the second halves of 2022 (46.15%) and 2023 (51.63%). Strikingly, in the second half of 2024, GII.17[P17] became predominant, causing 75.28% of outbreaks. This shift was driven by a novel GII.17 variant (Romania-2021 like, subcluster C2), first detected in February 2024, which replaced the previous Kawasaki 308-like variant. The novel variant predominantly affected the 6-18 years age group (54.97%) and elementary schools (34.33%). Relative to Cluster D, this novel variant harbors five amino acid mutations in antigenic epitopes, one mutation in the histo-blood group antigen (HBGA) binding site, and two deletions. CONCLUSIONS: A novel GII.17 variant has overtaken GII.4 as the predominant norovirus strain in China since late 2024, underscoring the need for continued molecular surveillance.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Norovirus causes widespread outbreaks of acute gastroenteritis (AGE) across all age groups, yet the role and dynamics of non-GII.4 genotypes remain insufficiently characterized in China. The study was needed to document a reported resurgence of GII.17 norovirus and understand its public health implications.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This was a national observational study of norovirus outbreaks in China from January 2022 to December 2024, collecting outbreak data and specimens for genotyping and sequencing. The study covered multiple provinces and included 1,579 norovirus outbreaks, of which 1,225 were genotyped.
analysis.methods: Outbreak samples were tested using real-time RT-PCR, and GII.17[P17]-positive samples underwent sequencing and phylogenetic analysis to identify variants and mutations. Data were collected systematically across the study period.
analysis.main_results: Among 1,579 norovirus outbreaks, 1,225 were genotyped. GII.4 Sydney dominated in the second halves of 2022 (46.15%) and 2023 (51.63%), while GII.17[P17] became predominant in the second half of 2024, causing 75.28% of outbreaks.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The shift to GII.17[P17] was driven by a novel variant (Romania-2021 like, subcluster C2) first detected in February 2024, which replaced the previous Kawasaki 308-like variant. This variant harbored five amino acid mutations in antigenic epitopes, one mutation in the HBGA binding site, and two deletions.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The emergence of this novel GII.17 variant as the predominant strain in China since late 2024 highlights the need for continued molecular surveillance to inform outbreak response and vaccine development strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study relies on outbreak-based surveillance data, which may underrepresent sporadic cases and limit generalizability to non-outbreak settings. The evidence is moderate due to the observational design and potential sampling bias.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the resurgence of GII.17[P17] norovirus in China during 2024, analyzing 1,579 norovirus outbreaks from 2022 to 2024. Using real-time RT-PCR and sequencing, the authors found that GII.17[P17] became the predominant genotype in the second half of 2024, accounting for 75.28% of outbreaks, surpassing the previously dominant GII.4 Sydney. The shift was attributed to a novel GII.17 variant (Romania-2021 like, subcluster C2) first detected in February 2024, which harbored mutations in antigenic epitopes and the HBGA binding site. The variant predominantly affected children aged 6-18 years and elementary schools. These findings underscore the importance of ongoing molecular surveillance to track emerging norovirus variants and guide public health interventions.

papers.full_text: Abstract Cruise ships are highly susceptible to rapid norovirus outbreaks, particularly in high-density recreational venues like swimming pools where hygiene protocols are difficult to enforce. Traditional quantitative microbial risk assessments are often retrospective and typically evaluate single transmission vectors, failing to capture the complex nature of different transmission pathways. To address this operational gap, this paper presents a novel, sensor-driven hybrid framework for the short-term risk assessment of norovirus transmission in maritime recreational water facilities. The proposed framework assesses multiple exposure routes by integrating a knowledge-based fuzzy inference system for primary waterborne transmission with a stochastic Agent-Based Model to quantify secondary fomite-mediated exposure via shared surfaces. Validated against a documented historical outbreak, the framework successfully synthesized these independent vectors to calculate a predicted risk of 77.0%, demonstrating high alignment with the historical ground-truth risk of 79.3%. By transforming passive environmental sensor data into real-time, actionable biosecurity alerts, this framework offers a proactive and highly accurate decision-support tool for mitigating localized norovirus outbreaks before they escalate into ship-wide events. papers.title_original: Integrating Fuzzy Logic and Agent-Based Modeling for Norovirus Risk Assessment on Cruise Ships

analysis.research_question_and_background: Cruise ships face rapid norovirus outbreaks in high-density recreational venues such as swimming pools where hygiene protocols are difficult to enforce, creating a need for proactive risk assessment tools that capture complex transmission pathways.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study presents a sensor-driven hybrid framework integrating a fuzzy inference system and an agent-based model to assess multiple norovirus exposure routes in maritime recreational water facilities.
analysis.methods: The framework uses a knowledge-based fuzzy inference system for primary waterborne transmission and a stochastic agent-based model to quantify secondary fomite-mediated exposure via shared surfaces, validated against historical outbreak data.
analysis.main_results: The framework predicted a norovirus risk of 77.0%, closely aligning with the documented historical ground-truth risk of 79.3% during validation against a documented outbreak.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the framework as a novel proactive decision-support tool that transforms passive environmental sensor data into real-time biosecurity alerts, enabling mitigation of localized outbreaks before escalation.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This framework offers a practical approach for maritime biosecurity by providing actionable, real-time risk assessments to prevent ship-wide norovirus outbreaks through targeted interventions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is moderate due to reliance on a single historical outbreak for validation and the absence of broader environmental or operational variability testing.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces a sensor-driven hybrid framework combining fuzzy logic and agent-based modeling to assess norovirus transmission risks in cruise ship recreational water facilities. The framework integrates primary waterborne exposure and secondary fomite-mediated pathways, validated against a historical outbreak where it predicted a 77.0% risk versus a documented 79.3% ground-truth risk. By converting passive sensor data into real-time biosecurity alerts, the tool aims to enable proactive outbreak mitigation before escalation. While demonstrating high predictive alignment, the framework’s strength is limited by validation against a single outbreak and lack of testing across diverse environmental conditions.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 游轮在游泳池等高密度娱乐场所面临着快速的 诺如病毒 暴发,这些场所的卫生规程难以执行,因此需要主动风险评估工具来捕获复杂的 传播 路径。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究提出了一种传感器驱动的混合框架,集成了模糊推理系统和基于代理的模型,以评估海上休闲水上设施中的多个 诺如病毒 暴露路线。
elements_zh.methods: 该框架使用基于知识的模糊推理系统来分析主要水性 传播,并使用基于随机代理的模型来量化通过共享表面的二次污染物介导的暴露,并根据历史 暴发 数据进行验证。
elements_zh.main_results: 该框架预测 诺如病毒 风险为 77.0%,与记录的 暴发 验证过程中记录的历史真实风险 79.3% 密切相关。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将该框架解释为一种新颖的主动决策支持工具,可将被动环境传感器数据转换为实时生物安全警报,从而在升级之前缓解局部 暴发 的影响。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该框架通过提供可操作的实时风险评估,通过有针对性的干预措施来防止全船出现 诺如病毒 暴发,从而为海上生物安全提供了一种实用方法。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 由于依赖单个历史 暴发 进行验证并且缺乏更广泛的环境或操作变异性测试,证据强度中等。

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究提出了一种传感器驱动的混合框架,集成了模糊推理系统和基于代理的模型,以评估海上休闲水上设施中的多个 诺如病毒 暴露路线。
analysis_zh.methods: 该框架使用基于知识的模糊推理系统来分析主要水性 传播,并使用基于随机代理的模型来量化通过共享表面的二次污染物介导的暴露,并根据历史 暴发 数据进行验证。
analysis_zh.main_results: 该框架预测 诺如病毒 风险为 77.0%,与记录的 暴发 验证过程中记录的历史真实风险 79.3% 密切相关。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将该框架解释为一种新颖的主动决策支持工具,可将被动环境传感器数据转换为实时生物安全警报,从而在升级之前缓解局部 暴发 的影响。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该框架通过提供可操作的实时风险评估,通过有针对性的干预措施来防止全船出现 诺如病毒 暴发,从而为海上生物安全提供了一种实用方法。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 由于依赖单个历史 暴发 进行验证并且缺乏更广泛的环境或操作变异性测试,证据强度中等。

papers.title: Environmental prevalence of enteric viruses across the covid-19 pandemic: A three-year monitoring study.
papers.abstract: Enteric viruses are continuously excreted in high concentrations in human feces and are disseminated into aquatic environments through treated and untreated wastewater, much of which is ultimately discharged into coastal marine waters. Environmental surveillance of these pathogens may therefore reflect their circulation in human populations and serve as an early-warning tool for the emergence of new viruses or variants, as well as increased transmission of existing ones. In this study, we investigated the occurrence and molecular diversity of major gastroenteric viruses - adenovirus, noroviruses, rotavirus - together with other enteric viruses with variable clinical relevance, in coastal marine waters of Campania Region (Southern Italy). Viral prevalence was evaluated according to season, sampling year, and type of wastewater discharge. A total of 500 marine water samples were collected, of which nearly half (44.0%) tested positive for at least one viral target. Viral detection rates varied across years, presumably influenced by the epidemiological dynamics associated with the COVID-19 pandemic. Notably, phylogenetic analyses revealed that most environmental viral sequences were identical or closely related to strains previously identified in human clinical cases from the same geographical area, supporting a strong epidemiological link between human infections and environmental contamination. Overall, these findings underscore the value of integrated environmental surveillance for public health risk assessment within a One Health framework.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Enteric viruses are widely disseminated into aquatic environments via wastewater, yet their environmental prevalence and molecular diversity during and after the COVID-19 pandemic remained insufficiently characterized in coastal marine waters. The study aimed to assess the occurrence and genetic diversity of major gastroenteric viruses in coastal marine waters of Campania Region (Southern Italy) to inform public health surveillance.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This was a three-year environmental monitoring study conducted in the coastal marine waters of Campania Region, Southern Italy. A total of 500 marine water samples were collected over the study period to evaluate viral prevalence according to season, sampling year, and type of wastewater discharge.
analysis.methods: Marine water samples were analyzed for the presence of adenovirus, noroviruses, rotavirus, and other enteric viruses using molecular detection methods. Viral prevalence was assessed in relation to season, sampling year, and wastewater discharge type. Phylogenetic analyses were performed to compare environmental viral sequences with human clinical strains from the same geographical area.
analysis.main_results: Nearly half (44.0%) of the 500 marine water samples tested positive for at least one viral target. Viral detection rates varied across years, likely influenced by COVID-19 pandemic-associated epidemiological dynamics. Phylogenetic analyses showed that most environmental viral sequences were identical or closely related to strains previously identified in human clinical cases from the same region.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study demonstrates a strong epidemiological link between human infections and environmental contamination, supporting the use of environmental surveillance as an early-warning tool for emerging viruses or increased transmission. The molecular diversity observed in environmental samples reflects human circulation patterns, highlighting the value of integrated surveillance within a One Health framework.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support the integration of environmental surveillance of enteric viruses into public health risk assessment strategies, particularly for early detection of viral emergence or resurgence in coastal regions. The approach can inform targeted interventions and risk mitigation measures in wastewater management and coastal water quality monitoring.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on a single geographical region and the absence of direct clinical data linkage beyond phylogenetic comparisons. While the evidence is strengthened by phylogenetic analysis linking environmental and clinical strains, generalizability to other regions or viral types remains uncertain, warranting cautious interpretation.

analysis.summary_en: This three-year environmental monitoring study in Campania Region, Southern Italy, investigated the prevalence and molecular diversity of major gastroenteric viruses in coastal marine waters. Among 500 samples, 44.0% tested positive for at least one viral target, with detection rates varying across years likely influenced by COVID-19 pandemic dynamics. Phylogenetic analyses revealed that most environmental viral sequences closely matched strains from human clinical cases in the same area, indicating a strong link between human infections and environmental contamination. The study underscores the value of environmental surveillance as an early-warning tool for viral emergence or increased transmission within a One Health framework. While the findings support integrating environmental surveillance into public health risk assessment, limitations include the study's regional focus and lack of direct clinical data linkage beyond phylogenetic comparisons, which may affect generalizability.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 肠道病毒通过废水广泛传播到水生环境中,但在 COVID-19 大流行期间和之后,其环境 患病率 和分子多样性在沿海海水中的特征仍然不充分。该研究旨在评估坎帕尼亚地区(意大利南部)沿海水域主要胃肠病毒的发生和遗传多样性,为公共卫生提供信息 监测。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这是一项在意大利南部坎帕尼亚地区沿海水域进行的为期三年的环境监测研究。研究期间共采集了 500 个海水样本,根据季节、采样年份和废水排放类型对病毒 患病率 进行评估。
elements_zh.methods: 使用分子检测方法分析海水样本中是否存在腺病毒、诺如病毒、轮状病毒和其他肠道病毒。根据季节、采样年份和废水排放类型对病毒 患病率 进行评估。进行系统发育分析,以将环境病毒序列与来自同一地理区域的人类临床毒株进行比较。
elements_zh.main_results: 500 个海水样本中近一半 (44.0%) 的至少一种病毒目标检测呈阳性。病毒检出率多年来有所不同,可能受到与 COVID-19 大流行相关的流行病学动态的影响。系统发育分析表明,大多数环境病毒序列与先前在同一地区的人类临床病例中鉴定的毒株相同或密切相关。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究表明,人类感染与环境污染之间存在密切的流行病学联系,支持使用环境 监测 作为新出现病毒或增加的 传播 的预警工具。在环境样本中观察到的分子多样性反映了人类循环模式,凸显了综合 监测 在 One Health 框架内的价值。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现支持将肠道病毒的环境 监测 纳入公共卫生风险评估策略,特别是对于沿海地区病毒出现或死灰复燃的早期检测。该方法可以为废水管理和沿海水质监测方面的有针对性的干预措施和风险缓解措施提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性在于其重点关注单一地理区域,并且缺乏系统发育比较之外的直接临床数据联系。虽然通过将环境和临床毒株联系起来的系统发育分析加强了证据,但对其他地区或病毒类型的普遍性仍然不确定,需要谨慎解释。

papers.title: Research on Mathematical Modeling of Infectious Disease Spread on Cruise Ships
papers.abstract: Cruise ships, characterized by high density, enclosed environments and shared facilities, have become amplifiers for infectious disease outbreaks; however, predicting transmission in such settings remains challenging due to small initial case numbers. In this study, a mathematical modeling framework—including compartmental, small-world (SW), and scale-free (SF) network models—was developed to analyze the dynamics of hantavirus and norovirus transmission on recent cruise ship outbreaks. The results show that when the initial number of exposed or infected individuals is extremely small (e.g., 1–2 persons), disease spread is dominated by stochasticity, causing substantial variation between individual simulations and mean model predictions. Notably, SF networks exhibited lower transmission risk under these conditions, contradicting the theoretical expectation that when the population is large, SF networks facilitate the spread of disease. The compartmental model, while consistent with average simulation outcomes, failed to reliably predict any single outbreak event. In conclusion, for closed environments such as cruise ships with very few initial cases, stochastic variability is essential, and single-outbreak outcomes should be understood as highly contingent rather than deterministically predictable.

source_records.abstract: Cruise ships, characterized by high density, enclosed environments and shared facilities, have become amplifiers for infectious disease outbreaks; however, predicting transmission in such settings remains challenging due to small initial case numbers. papers.abstract_zh: 邮轮以高密度、封闭环境、共享设施为特点,成为传染病的放大器暴发;然而,由于初始病例数较少,在这种情况下预测 传播 仍然具有挑战性。在这项研究中,开发了一个数学建模框架——包括隔室、小世界(SW)和无标度(SF)网络模型——来分析最近的游轮暴发上的汉坦病毒和诺如病毒 传播的动态。结果表明,当初始暴露或感染个体数量极少(例如 1-2 人)时,疾病传播以随机性为主,导致个体模拟与平均模型预测之间存在巨大差异。值得注意的是,SF 网络在这些条件下表现出较低的 传播 风险,这与当人口较多时 SF 网络促进疾病传播的理论预期相矛盾。隔室模型虽然与平均模拟结果一致,但无法可靠地预测任何单个 暴发 事件。总之,对于初始病例很少的游轮等封闭环境,随机变异至关重要,并且单一 暴发 结果应被理解为高度偶然的而不是确定性可预测的。

papers.title: Diagnostic and Microbiological Impact of Multiplex Syndromic Testing for Acute Infectious Gastroenteritis in a Regional Laboratory Network: A Real-World Before–After Study
papers.abstract: Acute infectious gastroenteritis (AIG) is caused by diverse bacterial and viral enteric pathogens with overlapping clinical presentations, limiting conventional pathogen-directed workflows. This retrospective before–after study evaluated the diagnostic, microbiological, operational, and economic impact of multiplex molecular syndromic testing for AIG within a regional hub-and-spoke laboratory network in Italy. Two 19-month periods were compared: a pre-implementation period based on conventional diagnostics and a post-implementation period using multiplex syndromic panels as first-line tests. Diagnostic investigations totalled 25,574 before and 24,509 after implementation. Overall test positivity increased from 5.43% to 11.59% (p < 0.001), with significant increases for bacterial and viral targets. Pathogen detection events increased from 1388 to 2839, including broader detection of Campylobacter spp., Shigella spp./enteroinvasive Escherichia coli (EIEC), Yersinia enterocolitica, Aeromonas spp., Astrovirus, Sapovirus, and Norovirus genogroups. Mean turnaround time decreased from 63 to 47 h from sample collection and from 56 to 41 h from laboratory check-in. Although direct diagnostic costs increased moderately, total laboratory costs decreased when personnel costs were included, and cost per diagnostic detection declined from €233.80 to €120.86. Multiplex syndromic testing improved microbiological detection, diagnostic efficiency, turnaround time, and laboratory organisation in routine AIG diagnosis.

analysis.summary_en: This real-world before–after study evaluated the impact of introducing multiplex molecular syndromic testing for acute infectious gastroenteritis (AIG) in a regional Italian laboratory network by comparing 19-month periods before and after implementation. The study found that multiplex testing increased overall test positivity from 5.43% to 11.59%, doubled pathogen detection events, and reduced mean turnaround times from 63 to 47 hours from sample collection and from 56 to 41 hours from laboratory check-in. Additionally, the cost per diagnostic detection decreased from €233.80 to €120.86. The authors conclude that syndromic testing improves microbiological detection and diagnostic efficiency in routine AIG diagnosis. However, the retrospective design and single-region setting limit causal inference and generalizability.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 急性传染性胃肠炎(AIG)在不同的细菌和病毒病原体中呈现出重叠的临床特征,这使传统的病原体特异性诊断工作流程变得复杂,并可能导致诊断不足或延迟检测。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 一项回顾性前后研究评估了在意大利区域中心辐射实验室网络中实施 AIG 多重分子综合征检测的影响,比较了实施前后两个 19 个月的时间段。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究将传统诊断与一线多重综合征组合进行比较,测量两个时期的诊断调查、测试阳性、病原体检测事件、周转时间和成本。
elements_zh.main_results: 总体检测阳性率从 5.43% 增加至 11.59% (p < 0.001),其中细菌和病毒目标显着上升;病原体检测事件从 1388 件增加到 2839 件,样本采集后的平均周转时间从 63 小时减少到 47 小时,实验室登记后的平均周转时间从 56 小时减少到 41 小时,每次诊断检测的成本从 233.80 欧元下降到 120.86 欧元。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为证明多重综合征检测可增强常规 AIG 诊断 中的微生物检测和诊断效率,代表着区域实验室网络中从传统工作流程到综合征检测的新转变。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,采用多重综合征检测可以提高病原体检测广度、减少诊断延迟并降低每次检测成本,为实验室工作流程优化提供信息,并有可能改善 AIG 的患者管理。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的回顾性前后设计和单区域实施限制了因果推断和普遍性,但多个结果的一致改进加强了证据基础。

papers.title_zh: 区域实验室网络中急性传染性胃肠炎多重综合症检测的诊断和微生物学影响:真实世界的前后研究
papers.source_body_en: Acute infectious gastroenteritis (AIG) is caused by diverse bacterial and viral enteric pathogens with overlapping clinical presentations, limiting conventional pathogen-directed workflows. This retrospective before–after study evaluated the diagnostic, microbiological, operational, and economic impact of multiplex molecular syndromic testing for AIG within a regional hub-and-spoke laboratory network in Italy. Two 19-month periods were compared: a pre-implementation period based on conventional diagnostics and a post-implementation period using multiplex syndromic panels as first-line tests. Diagnostic investigations totalled 25,574 before and 24,509 after implementation. Overall test positivity increased from 5.43% to 11.59% (p < 0.001), with significant increases for bacterial and viral targets. Pathogen detection events increased from 1388 to 2839, including broader detection of Campylobacter spp., Shigella spp./enteroinvasive Escherichia coli (EIEC), Yersinia enterocolitica, Aeromonas spp., Astrovirus, Sapovirus, and Norovirus genogroups. Mean turnaround time decreased from 63 to 47 h from sample collection and from 56 to 41 h from laboratory check-in. Although direct diagnostic costs increased moderately, total laboratory costs decreased when personnel costs were included, and cost per diagnostic detection declined from €233.80 to €120.86. Multiplex syndromic testing improved microbiological detection, diagnostic efficiency, turnaround time, and laboratory organisation in routine AIG diagnosis.
papers.abstract_zh: 急性感染性胃肠炎 (AIG) 由多种细菌和病毒肠道病原体引起,具有重叠的临床表现,限制了传统的病原体导向的工作流程。这项回顾性前后研究评估了意大利区域中心辐射实验室网络中 AIG 多重分子综合征检测的诊断、微生物学、操作和经济影响。比较了两个 19 个月的时期:基于传统诊断的实施前时期和使用多重综合征组作为一线测试的实施后时期。实施前诊断调查总数为 25,574 例,实施后诊断调查总数为 24,509 例。总体检测阳性率从 5.43% 增加至 11.59% (p < 0.001),其中细菌和病毒目标显着增加。病原体检测事件从 1388 个增加到 2839 个,包括更广泛地检测弯曲杆菌属、志贺氏菌属/肠侵袭性大肠杆菌 (EIEC)、小肠结肠炎耶尔森氏菌、气单胞菌属、星状病毒、沙波病毒和 诺如病毒 基因组。样本采集的平均周转时间从 63 小时减少到 47 小时,实验室登记的平均周转时间从 56 小时减少到 41 小时。尽管直接诊断成本略有增加,但考虑到人员成本后,实验室总成本有所下降,每次诊断检测的成本从 233.80 欧元下降至 120.86 欧元。多重综合症检测改善了常规 AIG 诊断 中的微生物检测、诊断效率、周转时间和实验室组织。

papers.title: Direct estimation of genotype fitness from time series
papers.abstract: Heterogeneous adapting populations, whether in laboratory evolution experiments or global-scale pandemics, experience complex evolutionary dynamics due to the interplay of selection, mutation, and stochasticity. Inference of individual genotypes' fitnesses therefore becomes difficult, especially when many lineages are competing and data are noisy. Existing fitness inference methods tend to rely on assumptions on the fitness landscape's maximum order of epistasis, or they require complicated iterative optimization algorithms to converge on fitness estimates. Here, we show that fitness landscapes can be computed from time series data, without any restrictions on epistatic order or iterative optimization, using a simple, closed-form mathematical expression that is easily implemented with standard matrix operations used commonly in linear algebra. We demonstrate successful fitness inference from noisy in silico evolutionary dynamics from four different noisy microscopic processes, including Wright-Fisher, Moran, ProSeD (serial dilution), and barcoded passage simulations. Then, we illustrate the broad applicability of the equation to five experimental time series datasets, including barcoded yeast evolution experiments, murine norovirus-1 serial passage experiments, and SARS-CoV-2 global genomic prevalence data. Our formula successfully infers fitnesses for even for rare genotypes several orders of magnitude less prevalent than top lineages, works with both laboratory evolution and epidemiological data, and can be implemented in most modern scientific programming languages.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the challenge of inferring the fitness of individual genotypes in heterogeneous adapting populations, where selection, mutation, and stochasticity complicate evolutionary dynamics. Existing methods often impose restrictive assumptions on epistasis or require computationally intensive iterative optimization, leaving a gap for simpler, more generalizable approaches.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The authors developed a closed-form mathematical expression to compute fitness landscapes directly from time series data without restrictions on epistasis order or iterative optimization. They validated the method using noisy in silico evolutionary dynamics from four microscopic processes and applied it to five experimental time series datasets, including barcoded yeast evolution, murine norovirus-1 serial passage, and SARS-CoV-2 genomic prevalence data.
analysis.methods: The core method involves deriving a closed-form expression for fitness inference from time series data using standard matrix operations in linear algebra. This approach was tested on simulated data from Wright-Fisher, Moran, ProSeD (serial dilution), and barcoded passage models, as well as experimental datasets spanning laboratory evolution and epidemiological surveillance.
analysis.main_results: The formula successfully inferred fitnesses for rare genotypes several orders of magnitude less prevalent than dominant lineages. It performed robustly across diverse datasets, including barcoded yeast evolution experiments, murine norovirus-1 serial passage experiments, and SARS-CoV-2 global genomic prevalence data, demonstrating broad applicability.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret their findings as evidence that fitness landscapes can be computed directly from time series data without restrictive assumptions or iterative optimization, representing a methodological advance over existing approaches. The novelty lies in the simplicity and generality of the closed-form expression, which enables efficient fitness inference across varied evolutionary contexts.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This method enables direct estimation of genotype fitness from noisy time series data, which could improve surveillance of pathogen evolution, inform experimental evolution studies, and enhance understanding of adaptive dynamics in heterogeneous populations. Its applicability to both laboratory and epidemiological data broadens its utility for research and public health.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report limitations such as potential biases in time series data, the impact of sampling frequency, or the generalizability to highly structured fitness landscapes. The strength of evidence is high given the validation across multiple simulated and experimental datasets, but broader applicability requires further testing in diverse biological systems.

analysis.summary_en: This study introduces a closed-form mathematical expression to directly compute fitness landscapes from time series data, addressing limitations of existing methods that rely on restrictive epistasis assumptions or iterative optimization. The approach was validated using noisy simulations from four evolutionary models and applied to five experimental datasets, including barcoded yeast evolution, murine norovirus-1 serial passage, and SARS-CoV-2 genomic prevalence data. The formula accurately inferred fitnesses for rare genotypes and demonstrated broad applicability across laboratory and epidemiological contexts. The method represents a methodological advance by enabling efficient, assumption-free fitness inference, with potential implications for pathogen surveillance, experimental evolution, and adaptive dynamics research.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究解决了推断异质适应群体中个体基因型适应性的挑战,其中选择、突变 和随机性使进化动力学变得复杂。现有方法通常对上位性施加限制性假设或需要计算密集型迭代优化,从而为更简单、更通用的方法留下了空白。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 作者开发了一种封闭式数学表达式,可以直接从时间序列数据计算适应度景观,而不受上位顺序或迭代优化的限制。他们使用来自四个微观过程的噪声计算机进化动力学验证了该方法,并将其应用于五个实验时间序列数据集,包括条形码酵母 进化、小鼠 诺如病毒-1 连续传代和 SARS-CoV-2 基因组 患病率 数据。
elements_zh.methods: 核心方法涉及使用线性代数中的标准矩阵运算从时间序列数据导出用于适应度推断的封闭式表达式。该方法在来自 Wright-Fisher、Moran、ProSeD(连续稀释)和条形码传代模型的模拟数据以及涵盖实验室 进化 和流行病学 监测 的实验数据集上进行了测试。
elements_zh.main_results: 该公式成功地推断出稀有基因型的适应性,这些基因型的流行程度比优势谱系低几个数量级。它在不同的数据集上表现强劲,包括条形码酵母 进化 实验、小鼠 诺如病毒-1 连续传代实验和 SARS-CoV-2 全球基因组 患病率 数据,证明了广泛的适用性。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将他们的发现解释为证据,表明适应度景观可以直接从时间序列数据计算出来,无需限制性假设或迭代优化,这代表了现有方法的方法论进步。新颖之处在于封闭式表达的简单性和通用性,这使得能够在不同的进化背景下进行有效的适应性推断。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该方法能够从噪声时间序列数据中直接估计基因型适应性,这可以改进病原体 进化 的 监测,为实验 进化 研究提供信息,并增强对异质群体中适应性动态的理解。它对实验室和流行病学数据的适用性扩大了其在研究和公共卫生方面的用途。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 所提供的证据没有报告局限性,例如时间序列数据的潜在偏差、采样频率的影响或高度结构化的适应度景观的普遍性。鉴于多个模拟和实验数据集的验证,证据的强度很高,但更广泛的适用性需要在不同的生物系统中进行进一步测试。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the challenge of inferring the fitness of individual genotypes in heterogeneous adapting populations, where selection, mutation, and stochasticity complicate evolutionary dynamics. Existing methods often impose restrictive assumptions on epistasis or require computationally intensive iterative optimization, leaving a gap for simpler, more generalizable approaches.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The authors developed a closed-form mathematical expression to compute fitness landscapes directly from time series data without restrictions on epistasis order or iterative optimization. They validated the method using noisy in silico evolutionary dynamics from four microscopic processes and applied it to five experimental time series datasets, including barcoded yeast evolution, murine norovirus-1 serial passage, and SARS-CoV-2 genomic prevalence data.
analysis_en.methods: The core method involves deriving a closed-form expression for fitness inference from time series data using standard matrix operations in linear algebra. This approach was tested on simulated data from Wright-Fisher, Moran, ProSeD (serial dilution), and barcoded passage models, as well as experimental datasets spanning laboratory evolution and epidemiological surveillance.
analysis_en.main_results: The formula successfully inferred fitnesses for rare genotypes several orders of magnitude less prevalent than dominant lineages. It performed robustly across diverse datasets, including barcoded yeast evolution experiments, murine norovirus-1 serial passage experiments, and SARS-CoV-2 global genomic prevalence data, demonstrating broad applicability.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret their findings as evidence that fitness landscapes can be computed directly from time series data without restrictive assumptions or iterative optimization, representing a methodological advance over existing approaches. The novelty lies in the simplicity and generality of the closed-form expression, which enables efficient fitness inference across varied evolutionary contexts.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This method enables direct estimation of genotype fitness from noisy time series data, which could improve surveillance of pathogen evolution, inform experimental evolution studies, and enhance understanding of adaptive dynamics in heterogeneous populations. Its applicability to both laboratory and epidemiological data broadens its utility for research and public health.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report limitations such as potential biases in time series data, the impact of sampling frequency, or the generalizability to highly structured fitness landscapes. The strength of evidence is high given the validation across multiple simulated and experimental datasets, but broader applicability requires further testing in diverse biological systems.

papers.title_zh: 从时间序列直接估计基因型适合度
papers.source_body_en: Heterogeneous adapting populations, whether in laboratory evolution experiments or global-scale pandemics, experience complex evolutionary dynamics due to the interplay of selection, mutation, and stochasticity. Inference of individual genotypes' fitnesses therefore becomes difficult, especially when many lineages are competing and data are noisy. Existing fitness inference methods tend to rely on assumptions on the fitness landscape's maximum order of epistasis, or they require complicated iterative optimization algorithms to converge on fitness estimates. Here, we show that fitness landscapes can be computed from time series data, without any restrictions on epistatic order or iterative optimization, using a simple, closed-form mathematical expression that is easily implemented with standard matrix operations used commonly in linear algebra. We demonstrate successful fitness inference from noisy in silico evolutionary dynamics from four different noisy microscopic processes, including Wright-Fisher, Moran, ProSeD (serial dilution), and barcoded passage simulations. Then, we illustrate the broad applicability of the equation to five experimental time series datasets, including barcoded yeast evolution experiments, murine norovirus-1 serial passage experiments, and SARS-CoV-2 global genomic prevalence data. Our formula successfully infers fitnesses for even for rare genotypes several orders of magnitude less prevalent than top lineages, works with both laboratory evolution and epidemiological data, and can be implemented in most modern scientific programming languages.

Updated: 4:04 PM EDT Jul 17, 2026 Editorial Standards i The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration and other state public health officials on Thursday linked an outbreak of cyclosporiasis to iceberg lettuce that Taylor Farms supplied to Taco Bell.Earlier this week, the CDC issued a multistate notice for cyclospora, a foodborne parasite that gets into people’s bodies, particularly their gut, and causes a diarrheal illness.The CDC is more likely to issue an outbreak notice when the level of public health concern is higher and the public threat is specific, according to its guidelines. The notice was the eighth the CDC issued this year so far, according to its data.More than 1,600 people reported getting sick after eating at Taco Bell locations in Indiana, Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio and West Virginia. The FDA traced back a single supplier of the iceberg lettuce from Mexico used by these Taco Bell locations. Taco Bell is working to stop using this lettuce. The CDC is still investigating other outbreaks and illnesses of cyclosporiasis nationally that are unrelated to this outbreak. The Get the Facts Data Team analyzed data on CDC multistate foodborne outbreak notices issued since 2006 to determine which germs caused the most notices and which are commonly linked to illness, hospitalizations and deaths. How many multistate foodborne outbreak notices has the CDC issued since 2006?Since 2006, the CDC has issued 231 multistate foodborne outbreak notices, letting the public know what actions they can take to stay healthy. Salmonella was the foodborne germ with the most outbreak notices, at 116. Escherichia coli, also known as E. coli, had the second-most outbreak notices with 54, and Listeria had 38.How many cyclosporiasis outbreaks have there been previously? The Cyclospora surge is the first cyclosporiasis outbreak for which the CDC has issued a notice this year. The last time the health agency issued an outbreak notice for cyclosporiasis was in 2020 for a bagged salad mix. In total, there have been 10 outbreak notices for the parasite since 2006.What germs commonly cause foodborne illnesses? About 48 million people get sick from a foodborne illness each year, with about 128,000 ending up hospitalized and 3,000 deaths, according to the CDC. Norovirus is the leading foodborne germ that causes illness in the U.S. The highly contagious germ, sometimes called the "stomach flu" or "stomach bug," causes vomiting and diarrhea. Norovirus is also the leading cause of foodborne illness that results in hospitalization. But it’s Salmonella that leads in deaths in the U.S. and causes about 1.35 million infections every year. And what's *** feature of all of those items is they have rough irregular surfaces. So they're very difficult to fully clean. That's the biggest challenge. That's the biggest opportunity to reduce the risk of getting this infection. Well, people should not use things like bleach or other to clean surfaces. What they need to do is do other than just apply running water. They need some physical contacts against the food items themselves to clean the surfaces. So washing very well with clean water and then manually cleaning the fruit or vegetables generally will prevent the transmission. It's not clear if it's coming from farms. It's not clear if there are other sources involved. But again, the general approach of washing it vigorously with water and then manually cleaning the food items is the best strategy that we have. There's also not human to human transmission. The way this spreads is from *** person having diarrhea and some of that material getting into either food prep or food service. That's the way it can transmit. Um, in general, the, the therapy is to rest and keep up with your fluids. You wanna be very selective you're, you're using over the counter medication, medication that slows the diarrhea. You don't want to retain um the parasite in your system. analysis.brief_en: On July 17, 2026, U.S. health authorities linked a multistate outbreak of cyclosporiasis to iceberg lettuce supplied by Taylor Farms to Taco Bell, with more than 1,600 illnesses reported across Indiana, Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio, and West Virginia. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) issued its eighth multistate foodborne-outbreak notice of the year, underscoring heightened public-health concern. Cyclospora, a foodborne parasite, causes explosive watery diarrhea and typically resolves without treatment, though antibiotics are needed in severe cases. Separately, CDC data show Salmonella remains the leading cause of foodborne deaths and outbreak notices, while norovirus causes the most illnesses and hospitalizations annually.

news.title: How Can You Avoid Norovirus 2026? - The People's Pharmacy

news.excerpt_original: How Can You Avoid Norovirus 2026? The People's Pharmacy

news.content: Norovirus is nasty! You do not want to catch this “stomach flu.” It is also called “winter vomiting disease” and “cruise ship virus.” This pathogen is incredibly contagious and is circulating far and wide. We know that people are fed up with viruses: coronaviruses, flu viruses, cold viruses, HMPV, etc. But norovirus 2025 is nasty! Public health authorities are reporting that cases are up substantially from previous years. They are beginning to suspect that a new strain is responsible for this stomach bug: GII.17[P17]. There are other strains out there, but this one has seemingly taken over. The most recent notice from the CDC is dated January 2, 2025, but there is not a lot of detailed information about what’s in store for us over the next several weeks. Given the latest trends, however, it looks like we are in for a literal S**T storm! Where Are People Suffering? Cruise ships are reporting an uptick in cases. And some early warning signs are flashing on land as well. I am especially fond of WastewaterScan’s dashboard. These are the folks who monitor sewage around the country. They have reported that SARS-CoV-2, RSV and influenza A are at high levels. They have also reported that norovirus is “high” and has been trending up over the last 3 weeks. Judging from their map, this intestinal virus is pretty well distributed around the United States. I fear that the CDC won’t have solid data for another week or so, but it would be prudent to be careful. More about that shortly. You will not easily forget a run-in with this intestinal apocalypse! Just contemplate the term “projectile vomiting.” Perhaps you have heard the expression “gut wrenching.” It is usually reserved for an emotionally challenging experience. I would like to suggest that you take that phrase literally. It should give you pause if you think norovirus is no big deal. What Are the Symptoms of Norovirus? Symptoms come on suddenly with severe vomiting and diarrhea. Victims may also have headaches, stomach cramps and fever. Reading about such symptoms doesn’t tell the real story, though. Here is what readers of our newsletter report: Mike gives you a sense of what this virus is like: “It does come on quickly, believe me! Hopefully you are near a bathroom when it strikes...like within a few steps! It is the only time in my life where I had to alternate sitting and kneeling for hours, outside of church. “I did not leave the bathroom for a few hours out of fear. Dehydration is very thorough and no doubt dangerous for many. If you first experience symptoms at home, cancel any plans for a few days because it will hunt you down. “This virus is almost impossible to avoid if you are caring for infected kids. It was 8 years ago and I still use it as a relative measure. “Well compared to noro....” You get the idea.” Pat also describes an intestinal “apocalypse”: “After Christmas dinner at our daughter’s house, EVERYONE that was there came down with norovirus! My husband hadn’t been feeling well (nausea) and went to bed early. “By 9:00 pm my nausea, stomach cramping, vomiting and diarrhea started with a cataclysmic explosion! If I’d known what was happening, I would have stayed on the toilet with a large bowl in my lap. I had no idea this would go on for 5 hours! Every time I had to vomit, the diarrhea would activate at the same time. “I would not wish this on my worst enemy, and I pray to God that I never get it again!” C. tells what happens when you are close to cruise ships: “I lived in the Caribbean with my office right on the harbor. One day I bought a salad from a fast food place where a lot of the cruise ship crew ate. The next day I thought I was going to die. I certainly wished I would because I was unbelievably miserable. “I literally could not even drink water the first day because it would trigger vomiting and dry heaves, coming out all ends. The second day I could suck on ice chips, and the third day I could take small sips of ginger ale. I was incredibly weak so I could barely stand up. It was the most excruciating stomach pain I’ve ever had in my life.” D. has another way to describe a norovirus attack: “I’m currently recovering from what is probably norovirus. I don’t know where I caught it but had been to the pharmacy, chiropractor and grocery store. Intestinal tsunami is a perfect description for the abdominal pain and the projectile vomiting.” K. demonstrates how contagious this bug can be: “Norovirus is as contagious as they say. I caught it and became very ill. I went to bed early because I didn’t feel well but had to get up because of the vomiting and extreme diarrhea. “On the way back from the bathroom, I passed out and woke up on the floor. I called the doctor in the morning. She advised hospitalization or Gatorade. My neighbor went to the store for me to get the Gatorade, but I didn’t realize how contagious norovirus is. She caught it from the money I gave her for the purchase!” As you can imagine, a condition that causes severe diarrhea and projectile vomiting could spread a lot of virus around. What’s more, it takes only a few viral particles to infect someone. How Do People “Catch” Norovirus? - “While sick, they shed billions of tiny viral particles in their stool and vomit. It takes a very small amount—as few as 18 viral particles—to make another person sick. People can get sick if they are exposed to a tiny amount of stool or vomit from an infected person. - They are most contagious when sick with vomiting and diarrhea, but may also infect others before symptoms start and after they feel better. - Because symptoms come on suddenly, an infected person who vomits in a public place may expose many people.” “Norovirus is hard to kill and stays on food, kitchen surfaces, and utensils. It can - Remain infectious on foods even at freezing temperatures and until heated above 140°F. - Stay on countertops and serving utensils for up to 2 weeks. - Resist many common disinfectants and hand sanitizers.” Can You Catch Norovirus From the Air? The CDC emphasizes that you can get norovirus by “touching surfaces or objects contaminated with norovirus and then putting your unwashed fingers in your mouth.” What the CDC does not mention is airborne transmission. The National Health Service (NHS) in the UK offers a somewhat different perspective, though. It does list contaminated food as one source of spread. The NHS also describes touching contaminated surfaces or objects. But here is the big difference between the US public health services and the NHS: “Norovirus spreads very easily in public places such as hospitals, nursing homes and schools. “You can catch it if small particles of vomit or stools (poo) from an infected person get into your mouth through: “• close contact with someone with norovirus who may breathe out small particles of the virus that you then inhale” We interpret that to mean that it is possible to breathe in norovirus...much as you might breathe in other viruses such as influenza or SARS-CoV-2. The only difference is that those are respiratory viruses, whereas norovirus is a viral infection that causes intestinal nastiness. How Can You Avoid Norovirus? There is no cure for norovirus. The only treatment is hydration. Some people become so dehydrated that they need intravenous fluids. That’s why prevention is the most effective strategy during an outbreak. That means being very careful about what you put in your mouth. Food or beverages that are touched by anyone who also handles money could easily be contaminated. That is why I have written extensively about coffee cups and dirty money at this link. It never fails to astonish me how many people push back about my cautions. Public restrooms pose a huge risk for infection. Knobs, door handles and almost any object in a public rest room should be treated as if it were nuclear waste. Hand sanitizer is not a substitute, unless it follows at least 20 to 30 seconds of scrubbing with soap and water. And if you walk into a public restroom where someone had either projectile vomiting or intense diarrhea, it is entirely possible that you will be exposed to the virus by just breathing the air. I know you hate the idea of masking...but you will hate the idea of vomiting even more! To prevent the spread of norovirus, conscientious hand washing is critical. Actually, that is an understatement! You cannot be too scrupulous in your hand hygiene! Air quality may also be a factor. How Easily Do Viruses Spread? Several years ago, researchers at the University of Arizona studied the spread of viruses by using a bacteriophage virus that resembles norovirus in size and shape (Sassi, American Journal of Infection Control, July 1, 2015). They put the test virus, which is noninfectious but easily detected, on a single door knob or table at the start of several research days in office buildings and a health care facility in Tucson. Throughout each day, they sampled other surfaces such as light switches, tap handles, bed rails or computer equipment. Nearly two-thirds of the surfaces studied had been contaminated within the first few hours of the day. The lead researcher, Chuck Gerba, PhD, determined that washing hands and using disinfectant wipes could stop this predictable spread almost completely. All we need to do is convince everyone to use these simple strategies. As your mother probably told you countless times, wash your hands. Don’t rely on hand sanitizer, as it does not work well against this virus. Scrubbing with soap and water works better. The Nay Sayers! Please take a look at some of the comments. These folks do not believe in the germ theory of disease. Noah thinks we should strengthen our immune systems through exposure: “I am wondering if, as a culture, we are overindulging in the use of ‘sanitary procedures’ such as constant washing of hands, massive use (abuse?) of ‘hand sanitizer’ and effectively minimizing the activation of our immune systems. “I presume that, much like our muscles, if our immune systems aren’t regularly challenged, tested gently, and required to be active they will not be as strong as they should be when we are faced with insult.” Try selling that message to someone in the middle of a norovirus attack. There is growing evidence to suggest that “viral reactivation” may contribute to dementia and other horrific chronic ailments. And no one wants to “strengthen” the immune system by catching poliovirus, tuberculosis or Lyme disease. Here is Julie’s comment: “I notice that the people who are most susceptible to bacteria-borne illnesses are the ones who constantly use hand sanitizers, Clorox wipes on surfaces, and are plainly in terror of everything not completely sterilized. “I wash my hands with soap (but usually less than 10 seconds) after using the restroom, don’t own a bottle of hand sanitizer, and invoke the 5-10 second rule if something edible (like a cookie) hits a floor, etc. “I’m rarely ill or suffer stomach viruses or other nasty maladies. I suspect it’s because I’ve developed a healthy immune system over the years by not being a germ-o-phobe.” And here is a response to the nay sayers from Jas: “I’M OUTRAGED! The reason why viruses, germs, fungi & bacteria thrive in the first place is that their hosts of transmission are ignorant, inconsiderate, lazy humans. Yes, viruses will still survive and get people sick... but how hard is it to wipe Purell on your hands? Really? It takes 10 seconds! (And what exactly are you going to do with those extra 10 seconds of not cleaning your hands? Save humanity???) “I got h-o-s-p-i-t-a-l-i-z-e-d with the norovirus, which I did track to the grocery cart I had used. God knows what baby poop or snot germs were on the cart handle, but it cost me, you and everyone else over $1,000 in insurance costs and lost wages for the ambulance, IV, over-night hospital stay, etc., just because you slobs out there don’t give a damn and think you’re invincible...? (Whiskey!-Tango!-Foxtrot!) “We live in our culture where people make more of an effort and spend billions of dollars to kill body odor, than kill the germs that can make them horribly sick or kill you! I say, label these stubborn, inconsiderate morons as F.O.Gs (Friends of Germs!) “I vote for the “Germ-a-phobes.” I’d rather live with reasonable preventative steps to protect my health and my family’s health than die with the plague... just because there’s a plague of idiots out there.” Don’t Forget to Disinfect: Washing up may not be enough, since flushing the toilet can spread infectious droplets around the bathroom. Consequently, the CDC recommends that bathroom surfaces be cleaned frequently with a bleach-based cleanser to disinfect them. “After someone vomits or has diarrhea, always thoroughly clean and disinfect the entire area immediately: - Put on rubber or disposable gloves and wipe the entire area with paper towels, then disinfect the area using a bleach-based household cleaner as directed on the product label. - Leave the bleach disinfectant on the affected area for at least five minutes, then clean the entire area again with soap and hot water. Finish by cleaning soiled laundry, taking out the trash, and washing your hands. “To disinfect, use a chlorine bleach solution with a concentration of 1,000 to 5,000 ppm (5 to 25 tablespoons of household bleach [5% to 8%] per gallon of water) or use an EPA-registered disinfecting product against norovirus.” Don’t want to measure 25 tablespoons of household bleach? The CDC offers this: “3⁄4 cup of bleach plus 1 gallon of water” Always wear disposable gloves and a face mask when cleaning up after someone who has experienced an intestinal apocalypse. Once you have cleaned up the mess and wiped everything down with a dilute bleach solution and left it for five minutes: “Step 4 Clean all surfaces again with hot water and soap Step 5 – Remove your gloves, throw them away, and take out the trash Step 6 – Wash all laundry that may have vomit or poop on it with hot water and soap Step 7 – Wash your hands with soap and water” A sick person should not cook for or care for others, as that might spread norovirus. There are tens of millions of people taking medications that suppress their immune systems. Many of them are advertised on television these days. A study in Clinical Chemistry, Jan. 3, 2025 reveals that people with less vigorous immune systems may shed viruses for longer than infectious disease experts realize. Food should be cooked completely, and laundry should be washed thoroughly with very hot water. Dry thoroughly at high temperature. We hope you do not catch nasty noro! If you have ever experienced this intestinal apocalypse, please describe it for the people who think “germs” are no big deal. You may want to let friends and family members know that norovirus is out there and spreading fast. We would be very grateful if you shared this article with them. If you were to also suggest signing up for our newsletter at this link, we would be even happier. Thank you for your support! It was 8 years ago and I still use it as a relative measure. “Well compared to noro....” You get the idea.” Pat also describes an intestinal “apocalypse”: “After Christmas dinner at our daughter’s house, EVERYONE that was there came down with norovirus! Intestinal tsunami is a perfect description for the abdominal pain and the projectile vomiting.” K. demonstrates how contagious this bug can be: “Norovirus is as contagious as they say. I caught it and became very ill. I went to bed early because I didn’t feel well but had to get up because of the vomiting and extreme diarrhea. “On the way back from the bathroom, I passed out and woke up on the floor. She caught it from the money I gave her for the purchase!” As you can imagine, a condition that causes severe diarrhea and projectile vomiting could spread a lot of virus around. analysis.brief_en: Public health authorities are reporting a significant increase in norovirus cases, with a suspected new strain (GII.17[P17]) identified as the cause. The virus, known for its high contagion rate and severe symptoms including vomiting and diarrhea, is spreading rapidly across the United States, affecting both cruise ships and land-based communities. Wastewater monitoring indicates high levels of norovirus, with cases trending upwards over the past three weeks. The CDC's latest notice, dated January 2, 2025, provides limited detailed information, and more comprehensive data is expected soon. The article underscores the importance of preventive measures to mitigate the spread of this highly contagious virus, which can remain infectious on surfaces for up to two weeks and is resistant to many common disinfectants.

news.content_title: Princess Cruises ship docks at Port Canaveral after norovirus outbreak
news.content: The Caribbean Princess cruise ship has docked at Port Canaveral, concluding a cruise where a norovirus outbreak sickened more than 100 passengers and crew members . The 19-deck Princess Cruises ship entered Port Canaveral before dawn Monday, May 11, then docked at Cruise Terminal 6 by 5:15 a.m. The ship had embarked April 28 from Port Everglades in Fort Lauderdale on a nearly two-week voyage. By Thursday, May 7, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention said that 102 of 3,116 passengers reported falling ill with the gastrointestinal illness, along with 13 out of 1,131 crew members. The predominant symptoms of norovirus are diarrhea and vomiting. 90025760007 November 2024: Princess Cruises plans long-term presence at Port Canaveral as it bases first ship there To counter the norovirus outbreak, the CDC said Caribbean Princess crew members isolated ill passengers and crew, increased cleaning and disinfection procedures according to an outbreak prevention-response plan, and collected stool specimens from gastrointestinal illness cases for testing. After disembarking the ship Monday morning, Palm Harbor resident Elly Evans recalled how she fell ill. She said she started "feeling blue and sluggish" and developed a persistent headache — but she took Tylenol and chalked up her discomfort to travel. But shortly after receiving a Swedish massage, she suffered norovirus symptoms and was isolated in her cabin for the next four or five days before recovering. Evans said she felt fine Monday, and she praised Caribbean Princess personnel and their precautions: "When things happen like this, they use the whole crew. 'You wash down everything in this section.' 'You wash down everything in this section.' They're excellent." According to a Princess Cruises media statement, Bahamian port officials declined to grant clearance for the ship to dock at Nassau during the cruise "out of an abundance of caution for their community, particularly as the island prepares for upcoming local elections in the coming day." "While Princess regrets the disappointment this itinerary change may cause, the health and well-being of our guests, crew, and the communities we visit remains our highest priority. Princess guests will be compensated with onboard credit for the missed port, and any pre-purchased shore excursions for Nassau are being fully refunded," the statement said. Caribbean Princess was scheduled to undergo comprehensive cleaning and disinfection before her next departure, which was scheduled for 3:30 p.m. Monday, May 11, per Port Canaveral's cruise ship schedule. 76625912007 Caribbean Princess debuted at Port Canaveral in November 2024 as Princess Cruises' first homeported ship, offering itineraries to the Caribbean and Central America. The ship boasts 1,571 staterooms, including suites and mini-suites, along with 12 food and beverage venues; eight showrooms and lounges; five pools; seven hot tubs; a family splash zone; a spa and fitness center; a sports deck; upscale shopping; a casino; and centers for children and teens. In its media statement, Princess Cruises officials said the company has operated for decades under globally recognized health guidelines, working in close coordination with international and local authorities to safeguard guests and destinations. "No problem. 'Washie washie' is the word of the day," Marianne Congdon of Killingly, Connecticut, said of hand-washing Monday morning while awaiting ground transportation after debarking Caribbean Princess. The voyage marked her 47th cruise. Congdon said ship personnel initially announced that 14 passengers had fallen ill — and soon afterward, news stations started reporting more than 100 people had contracted norovirus. She said she did not see any ill passengers during her cruise. Rick Neale is a Space Reporter at FLORIDA TODAY, where he has covered news since 2004. Contact Neale at Rneale@floridatoday.com . news.content_title: 125 people sick in third Princess cruise norovirus outbreak this year
news.content: More than 120 people got sick in a norovirus outbreak aboard a Princess Cruises ship, marking the cruise line’s third this year. Among the 3,032 guests sailing on Ruby Princess, 102 reported being ill, along with 23 crew members, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention . Their main symptoms were diarrhea and vomiting. The health agency listed the impacted voyage dates as June 12 through July 2. The ship was sailing an Alaska and Canada voyage round-trip from San Francisco, according to CruiseMapper . More: Parasitic infection cases in Michigan explode in 10 days Princess said "a limited number of guests reported mild gastrointestinal illness" during the trip. "Our crew responded promptly by implementing enhanced sanitation protocols across the ship, and cases have since decreased and remain low," the company told USA TODAY in an emailed statement. The cruise line also isolated sick passengers and employees, along with other steps, the CDC said. The ship arrived in San Francisco as planned and "will be undergoing comprehensive cleaning and disinfection" before its next cruise, Princess added. The CDC has logged seven outbreaks of gastrointestinal illness on cruise ships that met its threshold for public notification so far in 2026. Two were due to E. coli, while the rest were caused by norovirus, including two on other Princess ships. There were 23 outbreaks that met that threshold in 2025, 18 of which were caused by norovirus, and the illness was behind 15 out of 18 outbreaks the prior year. While norovirus is frequently associated with cruise ships, those instances account for just 1% of all outbreaks reported . "(Outbreaks are) often taking place within the community, and oftentimes we don't know that they're happening," Sarah R. Michaels, an assistant professor at Tulane University’s Celia Scott Weatherhead School of Public Health and Tropical Medicine, previously told USA TODAY. "Really, when we have these areas where people ... are in really close contact, things like day care facilities, nursing homes and cruise ships, it’s more likely (to be) diagnosed, reported and brought to our attention." This story has been updated to add new information. Nathan Diller is a consumer travel reporter for USA TODAY based in Nashville. You can reach him at ndiller@usatoday.com. The outbreak was reported July 12 aboard the National Geographic Sea Bird, two days after the ship departed Sitka and three days before its scheduled arrival in Juneau on July 15, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention’s Vessel Sanitation Program (VSP) reported. The CDC said 18 of the ship’s 62 passengers had been struck down by the stomach bug, experiencing “vomiting [and] abdominal cramps.” 4 The outbreak was reported July 12 aboard the National Geographic Sea Bird, two days after the ship departed Sitka and three days before its scheduled arrival in Juneau on July 15. The source of the outbreak is still unknown, the CDC said. “VSP is remotely monitoring the situation, including review of the ship’s outbreak response and sanitation procedures,” health officials said in a statement. news.content: The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has reported a third gastrointestinal illness outbreak aboard the National Geographic Sea Bird in less than 3 months. The latest incident occurred during the vessel's July 10th–15th, 2026 voyage in Alaska, when 18 of the ship's 62 passengers experienced symptoms including abdominal cramps and vomiting. The expedition vessel, operated by National Geographic-Lindblad Expeditions , had previously recorded outbreaks during sailings from May 26th–31st and June 25th–30th . The first two incidents were confirmed as norovirus, while the cause of the most recent outbreak has not yet been identified, although the reported symptoms were consistent with the earlier cases. According to information provided to the CDC, the ship's crew implemented enhanced cleaning and disinfection procedures in accordance with the company's outbreak prevention and response plan. Additional measures included isolating affected passengers and crew, consulting with the CDC's Vessel Sanitation Program and collecting samples to assist with the investigation. The CDC continues to monitor the situation remotely. Nat Geo Sea Bird operates seasonal expedition cruises along the coasts of Alaska and British Columbia during the summer months. The vessel accommodates up to 62 passengers in 31 cabins and specializes in small-ship nature-focused itineraries. For more National Geographic Sea Bird incidents and accidents, see the ship's CruiseMinus page

news.source_body_en: The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has been notified of a third gastrointestinal illness outbreak aboard the expedition vessel National Geographic Sea Bird during a July 10–15, 2026 voyage in Alaska waters. Of the 62 passengers on board, 18 reported symptoms including abdominal cramps and vomiting. The vessel, operated by National Geographic–Lindblad Expeditions, had recorded two prior outbreaks in late May and late June, both confirmed as norovirus. The cause of the latest outbreak remains under investigation, though symptoms align with earlier cases. The ship’s crew has enacted enhanced cleaning protocols, isolated affected individuals, and consulted the CDC’s Vessel Sanitation Program, which continues to monitor the situation remotely. No fatalities have been reported.

news.content: Ruby Princess, a ship operated by Princess Cruises. — Wikimedia Commons - Z thomas At least 145 people were sickened in separate norovirus outbreaks aboard two cruise ships, federal health officials said. The outbreaks happened on the National Geographic Sea Bird and the Ruby Princess, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention said. Both outbreaks were reported to the CDC's Vessel Sanitation Program on Sunday, June 28. The main symptoms were vomiting and diarrhea. The CDC said norovirus caused the illnesses. On the Ruby Princess , 102 of 3,032 passengers reported being ill during the Princess Cruises trip, along with 23 of the 1,144 crew members. The Pacific Ocean voyage left San Francisco on Friday, June 12, traveled up to Alaska, and will end on Thursday, July 2, according to CruiseMapper . The Sea Bird saw illness reports from 19 out of 68 passengers, along with one of the 27 crew members. The Lindblad Expeditions voyage along the Alaskan coast started on Thursday, June 25, and ended on Tuesday, June 30. This was the second gastrointestinal illness outbreak on the Sea Bird in about a month. A dozen passengers and crew members became sick on a late May cruise, although the cause of that outbreak was unknown. National Geographic Sea Bird, a cruise ship operated by Lindblad Expeditions. — WIkimedia Commons - Dankarl Lindblad Expeditions, Princess Cruises, and the ships' crews increased cleaning procedures, isolated sick passengers and crew members, and consulted with the CDC. Princess Cruises also collected stool samples from sick people for testing. Cruise ships are required to report GI illness cases to the CDC. The agency defines acute gastroenteritis as three or more loose stools within 24 hours, or vomiting with another symptom such as abdominal cramps, diarrhea, fever, headaches, or muscle aches. news.content: Health Alaska cruise struck by third suspected norovirus outbreak in weeks The CDC said 18 of the 62 passengers on board developed symptoms including vomiting and abdominal cramps By The News Digital Published July 17, 2026 A cruise ship sailing in Alaska has reported its third gastrointestinal illness outbreak in just two months, with 18 passengers becoming ill during its latest voyage, according to the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). The outbreak occurred aboard Lindblad Expeditions' National Geographic Sea Bird during a cruise between 10 and 15 July. Advertisement The CDC said 18 of the 62 passengers on board developed symptoms including vomiting and abdominal cramps. According to the agency, the cause of the latest outbreak is currently listed as unknown. However, the ship's previous two outbreaks, reported in May and June, were confirmed to be norovirus, a highly contagious virus that causes vomiting and diarrhoea. In response, the cruise operator isolated sick passengers and crew, collected stool samples for testing, consulted with the CDC's Vessel Sanitation Program, and increased cleaning and disinfection procedures. The CDC said it is “remotely monitoring the situation,” including the cruise line's sanitation measures and outbreak response. The agency noted that cruise operators are required to report gastrointestinal illnesses quickly to help identify outbreaks and prevent further spread. It also said “norovirus is often a cause of gastrointestinal illness outbreaks on cruise ships,” although confirming the source of an outbreak can take time. Norovirus is commonly spread through contaminated food, water, surfaces or close contact with an infected person. news.content_original: Health Alaska cruise struck by third suspected norovirus outbreak in weeks The CDC said 18 of the 62 passengers on board developed symptoms including vomiting and abdominal cramps By The News Digital Published July 17, 2026 A cruise ship sailing in Alaska has reported its third gastrointestinal illness outbreak in just two months, with 18 passengers becoming ill during its latest voyage, according to the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). The outbreak occurred aboard Lindblad Expeditions' National Geographic Sea Bird during a cruise between 10 and 15 July. Advertisement The CDC said 18 of the 62 passengers on board developed symptoms including vomiting and abdominal cramps. According to the agency, the cause of the latest outbreak is currently listed as unknown. However, the ship's previous two outbreaks, reported in May and June, were confirmed to be norovirus, a highly contagious virus that causes vomiting and diarrhoea. In response, the cruise operator isolated sick passengers and crew, collected stool samples for testing, consulted with the CDC's Vessel Sanitation Program, and increased cleaning and disinfection procedures. The CDC said it is “remotely monitoring the situation,” including the cruise line's sanitation measures and outbreak response. The agency noted that cruise operators are required to report gastrointestinal illnesses quickly to help identify outbreaks and prevent further spread. It also said “norovirus is often a cause of gastrointestinal illness outbreaks on cruise ships,” although confirming the source of an outbreak can take time. Norovirus is commonly spread through contaminated food, water, surfaces or close contact with an infected person.
